title: Sales & Referrals
description: A CRM for water-treatment sales that connects customer referrals, demo appointments, rewards and rep coaching.
coverAlt: Illustration of a referral moving from a share link through eligibility and demo booking to reward review.

brief.contribution: I implemented referral validation and refined progress tracking so the sales team could see referral status in its dashboard.
brief.challenge: Referral volume alone says little about sales opportunity. A submission can stall before a demo, while duplicate or incomplete referrals create extra work and complicate reward decisions.
brief.decision: Keep customer sharing simple, then separate eligibility, booking and reward review. Each stage gives reps and managers a different decision to make.
brief.solution: Customer referral links connect to the CRM and sales calendar. Staff can monitor progress and review reward claims, while reps can practise conversations in a separate coaching tool.
brief.value: Make referral conversion easier to manage and give managers a clearer basis for reviewing incentive spend.

system.intro: Follow a referral from the share link to demo booking and reward review. Explore sales coaching as a separate tool for reps.

stages.label: Capture the referral
stages.component: A customer can submit a referral through a share link and check its progress in a tracker. The link keeps the referral connected to the person who made it.

stages.label: Review referral eligibility
stages.component: Check the submission against program rules and existing CRM records. A duplicate or ineligible referral needs a different response from a new opportunity.

stages.label: Book and track the demo
stages.component: Connect the referral to a CRM lead and calendar appointment so the rep can follow up and see whether the referral advanced.

stages.label: Review the reward
stages.component: Compare a claim with the referral’s recorded progress. Keeping rewards separate from submission helps staff apply program rules consistently.

stages.label: Coach the sales conversation
stages.component: Reps practise a scenario and receive feedback on different stages of the conversation, from opening to follow-up.

demonstrations.label: Sample scenario
demonstrations.alt: A sample referral path from share link to eligibility, demo booking and staff reward review.
demonstrations.caption: One customer referral, from the share link to a booked demo.
demonstrations.support: Staff can review the reward against the referral’s recorded progress.

technology: Next.js and Supabase support the CRM, referral links, booking records and reward review. OpenAI powers conversation practice. Water-air also exposes an integration endpoint that can accept Safiy session details and recordings for a lead or demo.

title: AFunTime
description: An event rental platform for managing quotes, delivery, booking approvals and allocation of physical inventory.
coverAlt: Representative artwork for AFunTime, an event rental booking and inventory platform.

brief.contribution: I built storefront and operations interfaces and implemented the inventory revision that checks eligibility and allocates individual units at approval.
brief.challenge: Overlapping requests can compete for the same equipment. A package may look available even though a single item prevents the business from fulfilling it.
brief.decision: Accept requests before committing stock. Review delivery and price, then recheck and reserve exact units at approval so the business can make a credible commitment.
brief.solution: Customers select packages and add-ons. Staff review quotes and stock, resolve shortages and confirm bookings against available equipment.
brief.value: Capture demand without overcommitting inventory, and give staff better visibility into the trade-offs behind each booking.

system.intro: Follow a rental request through pricing, capacity review and approval. See what changes when a required item is unavailable.

stages.label: Capture the rental request
stages.component: Customers choose a date, package and add-ons. Treat their submission as demand the business can review before committing equipment.

stages.label: Check available stock
stages.component: Compare the request with the actual units that can be assigned for the date. Flag a shortage before staff confirm a booking.

stages.label: Review price and delivery
stages.component: Staff review what the customer requested, the delivery requirements and the final quote before committing to the booking.

stages.label: Approve and allocate
stages.component: Recheck availability at approval and reserve individual units. If capacity has changed, bring the shortage back to staff for a decision.

stages.label: Confirm the booking
stages.component: Update the customer’s booking status and keep a payment record for staff to reconcile.

demonstrations.label: Sample scenario
demonstrations.alt: A fictional rental request for three chairs and one table with the table unavailable, followed by staff review and an updated booking.
demonstrations.caption: A customer requests a package while staff review what can be assigned.
demonstrations.support: A shortage is flagged before the booking is confirmed.

technology: Next.js powers the storefront and operations interface. Supabase and PostgreSQL manage bookings, permissions and stock. Booking automation rechecks availability and allocates specific units in a single database transaction when staff approve a booking.

title: Academia OS
description: A local-first AI workspace that organizes coursework and governs how AI agents propose changes to a student’s plan.
coverAlt: Representative artwork for Academia OS, a local-first AI workspace for students.

brief.contribution: I developed Study chat features and implemented improvements to how students review and edit proposed changes.
brief.challenge: Coursework spans syllabuses, files, calendars and several AI tools. An agent can find a deadline quickly, but an outdated source or unreviewed change can create more work for the student.
brief.decision: Tie proposals to source material and keep approval with the student. Give agents bounded access so using a new tool doesn’t mean handing over control of the plan.
brief.solution: Academia OS organizes coursework and coordinates the handoff from an AI agent’s proposal to student review and a recorded outcome.
brief.value: Reduce the effort of reconciling course information while keeping changes traceable and under the student’s control.

system.intro: Follow an AI proposal from a syllabus deadline to student approval or decline and the resulting plan.

stages.label: Organize course sources
stages.component: Keep course materials with their original context so a deadline can be traced back to the right document.

stages.label: Create an agent proposal
stages.component: An AI agent can suggest a task or deadline update for the student to review. The proposal identifies the change before anything is applied.

stages.label: Review and decide
stages.component: Check the date and source, then approve, edit where supported, or decline. The student controls whether the change goes ahead.

stages.label: Record the outcome
stages.component: Keep a record of the decision and show what changed. Declining a proposal leaves the plan unchanged.

demonstrations.label: Sample scenario
demonstrations.alt: A fictional syllabus deadline, an agent proposal, student review, and the recorded outcome or decline.
demonstrations.caption: A proposed task and the syllabus passage that supports it.
demonstrations.support: The student reviews the change before it appears in their plan.

technology: A Python core manages the local workspace, provenance and review logic. React runs in a Tauri desktop app. Agent adapters and permission grants govern how external tools access information and submit proposals for human review.
